boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all five frozen records in the Confederate Heartland Offensive. Preserve per-engagement dates; the live NPS campaign heading (June-October 1862) does not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives about 1,400 Confederates, as does the live NPS field; Cist says Forrest advanced with about two thousand men.
claims.rationale: Different retrospective estimates without inspected returns. The NPS narrative describes units joining on the way; no common counting point is established.

claims.value: NPS says the garrison camped in three locations around town; Cist says Lester had distributed the troops in different parts of town, and describes a camp guard behind a wagon barricade and rock ledges.
claims.rationale: Pre-attack dispositions and local cover, not a map-verified position or numerical terrain effect. The dispersion was a Union subordinate's choice before the raid.

claims.rationale: Inherited site function from a modern summary; no depot inventory was inspected.

claims.value: NPS says Forrest's cavalry surprised the Union pickets between 4:15 and 4:30 am; Cist says Forrest arrived about five o'clock and captured the pickets.
claims.rationale: Surprise is a summary judgment, not an inspected record of Union knowledge. The two clocks differ and are retained without reconciliation.

claims.value: NPS gives the major objective as striking Murfreesboro at dawn on July 13.
claims.rationale: Modern summary of purpose, not an inspected original order. Later diversion of Union forces is a campaign-contribution claim, not part of the tactical objective.

citations.quote: The major objective was to strike Murfreesboro, an important Union supply center on the Nashville & Chattanooga Railroad, at dawn on July 13.

claims.value: NPS places the garrison under Crittenden, who arrived July 12. Cist says Crittenden and Duffield returned on July 11, that neither assumed command, and that no one was in command.
claims.rationale: The arrival date and whether anyone exercised effective command conflict. Cist's judgment is an interested retrospective opinion. The frozen listed commander is not automatically assigned the Union result.

claims.value: The frozen result is Confederate victory; the live NPS result field reads Union Victory. The NPS narrative says all Union units surrendered to Forrest.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The live result field conflicts with the frozen record and its own narrative; the frozen value is retained and the conflict is not silently corrected.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,040 total (US 890; CS 150). The live NPS field reads 1350 total (US 1200; CS 150;).
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

claims.value: Cist reports about 600 horses and mules and large stores captured or destroyed; NPS says supplies were destroyed and track torn up.
claims.rationale: Post-outcome material consequences, not an inspected inventory. Cist's dollar valuation is not adopted as a measure.

open_questions: Original returns, the surrender count, casualty reconciliation, the Union command clock and the attack's exact opening time remain deferred after the bounded pass. The live result field conflict is not resolved.
NPS/CWSAC is one family; Cist is one interested retrospective Union staff history. Quoted reports and participant accounts inside Cist are not additional independently inspected families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
